newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea warns world labour leaders of deportation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea warns world labour leaders of deportation.

text.p: South Korea's immigration chief said on Friday 10 world trade leaders planning to visit the country would be allowed in, but warned they would be deported if they took part in strike-related protests.
Leaders of trade union organisations from around the world are to due to arrive in South Korea next week to show support for unions leading more than three weeks of strikes.

Yu Byong-rhang, director-general in charge of immigration at the Justice Ministry, said that four other international union leaders who left Seoul on Thursday had been warned about taking part in rallies during labour strife.
"Immigration officers will explain our laws to the new visitors on their arrival in view of the illegal activities by the four foreign union leaders," Yu told Reuters.
"There will first be warnings if they violate laws and if they continue not to heed them, then they will be deported," he said.
The Geneva-based International Federation of Commercial and Clerical Workers said a team of 10 unionists would maintain an international trade union presence in Seoul.
